Teach a sequence and recover its launch

html:
Correction sessions and learned-workflow flows

An explicit correction lets a person inspect a concrete tool call, choose accepted sources for its arguments and save a reviewed mapping. Starting a live correction requests cooperative Pause. Apply waits for accepted work to settle, saves the intent and adds a structured amendment when retry is appropriate. The Agent chooses its next operation through the normal execution path.

Learned workflows capture a reviewed order of successful calls and their exact mapping dependencies. Running one creates an ordinary task. Its downstream steps must use fresh results owned by that run. These artifacts have their own API and storage, separate from saved-request Workflows.

The Parameters manual explains the controls. Binding-review flows owns the separate successful-call approval surface, mapping storage, generation boundaries, matching and materialization. Successful-call approval alone does not request Pause or create a correction selection.

Data and owners

flowchart TD Person[Explicit user correction or teaching request] --> UI[Mapping dialogs and task shortcut] UI --> Routes[Strict correction and learned-workflow routes] Routes --> Correction[Corrections and task_corrections] Runs[Accepted run, invocations and exact receipts] --> Correction Parameters[Accepted parameters and explicit refresh choices] --> Correction Correction --> View[Masked inspection and preview token] View --> UI Correction --> Control[Native Pause and Resume owner] Correction --> Frozen[Private accepted correction snapshot in run] Correction --> Documents[Versioned mapping documents and immutable history] Correction --> Amendment[Idempotent structured amendment] Amendment --> Agent[Ordinary Agent decision and admission] Routes --> Teach[Learned workflow preview and launch] Runs --> Teach Documents --> Teach Teach --> Documents Teach --> Task[Ordinary queued task and dedicated conversation] Task --> Agent Agent --> Execute[Existing execution and receipt owners] Execute --> Runs
Owner Responsibility
parameter_mapping.js Passive task/call entry controls, persistent picker/editor, source choices, masked previews, explicit mutations, mapping library and learned-workflow dialogs. Shared field controls also serve binding reviews.
Mapping routes Strict bounded payloads, revision/idempotency fields and HTTP 409 translation for mapping/validation conflicts. Outer middleware owns authentication.
Corrections Current-attempt ownership, pause stamps, accepted source reconstruction, preview, frozen application intent, recoverable writes and cancellation.
task_corrections Passive task projection, failed-first call inventory, task-level session creation and exact call selection.
learned_workflows Ordered successful-call capture, exact reviewed mappings, explicit launch recovery and current-run producer rebinding.
MappingStore Detached current documents, immutable revisions and compare-and-set/idempotent writes on Controller RAM or standalone SQLite.

Public correction projections mask every argument scalar. Source choices contain catalog IDs, pointers, types and provenance; the server resolves their values. Reusable templates omit mapped values, and the template check rejects known protected values and credential literals. Explicit Reveal selected saved parameter uses the audited reveal endpoint and shows the current saved record. That disclosure does not itself replace accepted task inputs.

The private frozen snapshot belongs to the native run. A library rule records its template, source identities, scope and origin; it is not a copy of that private snapshot. Writes spanning the run, mapping library and steering journal are recoverable stages, not a single cross-store transaction.

Enter, pause and choose a call

sequenceDiagram actor Person participant UI as Task or call UI participant API as Correction service participant Docs as Session store participant Native as Native run owner UI->>UI: Render passive availability Person->>UI: Stop and map parameters UI->>API: Start task picker or exact-call correction API->>API: Lock queue and verify current run and bound mode API->>Docs: Reuse active session or save open session API->>Native: Request cooperative Pause when needed API->>Docs: Record ownership and pause stamp API-->>UI: Session, masked call inventory and readiness par Accepted work settles Native->>Native: Finish accepted work and release execution ownership and Person may choose a call Person->>UI: Select invocation UI->>API: Session revision, observed digest and selection key API->>Native: Verify exact invocation in current run API->>Docs: Attach call to the same session API-->>UI: Mapping editor projection end loop While mounted and awaiting readiness UI->>API: Inspect session API->>Native: Check paused checkpoint, pending work and lease API-->>UI: Ready only after settlement end

Passive task metadata reads accepted binding mode and scalar call information. RAM uses narrow state/receipt views; standalone SQLite extracts the required JSON fields and invocation order. Only registered concrete tools are offered. Failed calls sort first, then newer calls. Picker argument summaries are masked and bounded; aggregate calls are excluded in favor of their concrete children.

Task-level Start requires the request's current run, an eligible call and live work. It creates a session without a selected operation, or reopens the existing open/applying session. Per-call entry can select into that same picker. A conflicting second call cannot create another active correction for the run. Selection verifies the session revision and exact pending-invocation digest. An identical selection key replays the same intent; stale or foreign calls are rejected.

The session records whether it initiated Pause and the request's pause stamp. Already-paused work remains externally owned. An interrupted explicit Start can request Pause again. Apply readiness requires a paused checkpoint with no pending or unsettled work, no run lease owner and no running trace. Terminal work is ready for future-only saving. Choosing a call while work settles does not bypass this gate.

The browser keeps the same session through picker/editor transitions and reload. Closing removes the dialog and stops future polling; it does not cancel in-flight requests or release the server's pause. Picker callbacks check phase ownership before presenting late responses. Editor polling preserves the local draft and requires reopening if the session revision changes in another tab. Local edits invalidate previews, but inputs can remain editable during a request, so server token/revision checks remain the final authority.

Preview, freeze and apply

sequenceDiagram actor Person participant UI as Editor participant C as Corrections participant R as Native run participant D as Mapping documents participant N as Native controls Person->>UI: Choose sources and preview UI->>C: Revision, bindings and refresh intent C->>R: Reconstruct accepted inputs and exact receipts C->>C: Materialize, validate and detect future-only state C-->>UI: Masked preview, readiness and token Person->>UI: Apply reviewed intent UI->>C: Same intent and token with retained apply key C->>C: Lock queue and re-preview new intent C->>R: Claim maintenance lease and freeze accepted intent R-->>C: Saved snapshot, then release lease C->>D: Journal applying session and approved rule C->>D: Save rule revision idempotently alt Retry remains appropriate C->>D: Save explicit run selection C->>R: Add amendment once using session identity Note over C,R: Recheck source revisions before a new amendment C->>N: Resume if task remains paused else Save for future use C->>N: Release only a matching pause owned by this session end C->>D: Mark session applied last C-->>UI: Saved rule identity and final session Note over UI,N: Apply dispatches no tool, the Agent chooses what follows

Context reconstruction starts from the selected invocation's original proposed arguments, even when a previous mapping changed its executed arguments. It uses the accepted parameter snapshot and earlier owned receipts. Accept current saved values explicitly adds/refreshes named records for this correction before Apply freezes them; ordinary inspection does not silently refresh credentials.

Preview requires an open current revision. It resolves selected catalog IDs, builds a scope-specific rule, materializes arguments, validates the tool schema and checks template privacy. Its token covers session identity/revision, rule, source revisions, save-only state, evidence revision and remember intent. It also checks whether a later successful call already used the corrected arguments. Preview performs no persistence or dispatch.

New Apply repeats that validation under the task-queue lock and requires readiness. accept_snapshot takes a maintenance lease and saves the exact parameters, apply request and intent hash in accepted_parameter_corrections. The lease is released even on failure. A conflicting intent cannot replace an already frozen snapshot. If interruption occurs before the session reaches applying, inspection still recognizes the frozen intent and exposes its recovery request.

The subsequent journal stages use stable identities and distinct idempotency keys: applying session, saved rule, optional run selection, steering submission and final applied session. An exact Apply retry resumes those stages. A saved steering receipt prevents duplicate amendments. A one-time correction is scoped to the original run and its explicit selection claim; remembered rules may serve later matching tasks. Editing an existing reviewed rule retains its approval-generation boundary.

The browser exposes Finish applying correction for the saved recovery request. Recovery keeps the accepted snapshot and intended rule; it does not resolve today's saved credentials again. An applying session must finish that recovery rather than being discarded by Cancel. Storage/control errors can leave a recoverable intermediate stage, so a failed HTTP request does not imply that every preceding write was undone.

Future-only saving and cancellation

flowchart TD Inspect[Reconstruct selected call and settled evidence] --> Ended{Task terminal?} Ended -->|Yes| Future[Future-only mapping save] Ended -->|No| Unknown{Selected outcome unknown?} Unknown -->|Yes| Future Unknown -->|No| Later{Matching later successful call?} Later -->|Yes| Future Later -->|No| Retry[Require settled Pause before ordinary Apply] Future --> Remember{Remember enabled?} Remember -->|No| Reject[Reject one-time save-only intent] Remember -->|Yes| Save[Save rule without retry amendment] Save --> Owned{Session owns current matching pause?} Cancel[Cancel current open session] --> Owned Owned -->|Yes and settled| Resume[Release that pause through native control] Owned -->|Different or unowned pause| Preserve[Keep external pause] Owned -->|Owned pause still pending| Wait[Wait for settlement before release]

Unknown outcome means the earlier operation needs reconciliation; saving a future mapping does not authorize replay. Terminal work and later successful retries also use future-only saving. In that mode Remember must remain enabled, and no correction amendment or run selection is created.

Cancel accepts only the current open revision (or an identical completed cancel). It resumes only a pause initiated by this session whose current stamp still matches. A different pause is preserved. An owned pause that is still settling returns a conflict so the user can wait and cancel again. Closing the editor is independent of Cancel and leaves the persistent session available through Continue parameter mapping.

Teach a sequence and recover its launch

sequenceDiagram actor Person participant UI as Workflow dialogs participant W as Learned workflows participant D as Mapping store participant T as Conversations and tasks Person->>UI: Select successful calls in intended order UI->>W: Preview selected call IDs and title W->>W: Verify receipts, contracts, mappings and producer order W-->>UI: Ordered artifact and preview token Person->>UI: Save learned workflow UI->>W: Same selected sequence and token W->>W: Re-preview under queue lock W->>D: Save versioned workflow idempotently Person->>UI: Run learned workflow UI->>W: Current revision and retained launch key W->>W: Check EULA, enabled revision, binding and original scope W->>D: Recover or create launch identity W->>T: Recover or create dedicated conversation W->>T: Find existing task before creating an ordinary queued task W->>D: Persist task ID in launch record W->>T: Queue or start that task W-->>UI: Launch and conversation identity

Preview accepts one to 64 distinct successful calls in the selected order. It loads each concrete tool contract and exact mapping revision from recorded invocation metadata or an applied correction. Missing mapping history, a review requirement or a suspended revision prevents teaching. Every result-source producer must be from the same original run and occur earlier in the selection. All selected calls must share one workspace/Gateway scope.

Each step records its contract, reviewed argument template, effect, source receipt identity and optional learned mapping. It depends on the preceding selected step; result bindings additionally name their exact producer_step. Mapped values are removed from templates, including placeholder SSH roles. Required parameter names become symbolic task references. No branches or loops are inferred from the calls.

Save reconstructs the artifact and compares its token before writing. Launch requires EULA acceptance, enabled current revision and bound parameter mode. It uses current defaults in the original workspace/Gateway, embeds the reviewed plan and turns prompt rephrasing off. A stable launch identity determines its conversation. Task lookup includes archived tasks in that conversation before creation; the launch record stores the task identity before queue submission. Retrying the same launch key reuses that task and can retry queueing if it is still queued. A different workflow revision cannot reuse the same key. These stages do not execute a recorded tool call.

Resolve fresh producers during execution

flowchart TD Launch[Ordinary workflow task acceptance] --> Snapshot[Current accepted parameter snapshot] Plan[Reviewed ordered plan] --> Guard[Native workflow and mapping guards] Model[Agent proposes a tool call] --> Guard Guard --> Dependency{Required producers completed?} Dependency -->|No| Reject[Reject premature downstream mapping] Dependency -->|Yes| Step[Current step and exact reviewed mapping] Step --> Current[Verify current enablement, contract and suspension] Current --> Rebind[step_rule binds producer_step to this run and operation] Fresh[This run's completed claimed producer receipt] --> Rebind Rebind --> Resolve[Materialize exact source pointers and types] Snapshot --> Resolve Resolve --> Admission[Normal permission, step claim and execution admission] Admission --> Execute[Execute the Agent-selected call] Execute --> Receipt[Settle result under the claimed step] Receipt --> Fresh Receipt --> Next[Later dependent step or guarded completion]

native/learned_mappings.py rejects a call selecting a downstream learned mapping while dependencies remain incomplete, including reconciliation reads that might otherwise bypass step order. The current step supplies its reviewed mapping rather than an arbitrary library rule. Preparation checks the current rule's enablement/review state, revision suspension and tool contract before materialization.

step_rule copies the reviewed mapping and replaces each declared producer source with this conversation's run ID and the completed step's claimed operation ID. Missing/incomplete ownership is an error. Normal source resolution then requires the fresh owned receipt, exact pointer and compatible type. Old receipt identity is retained as teaching provenance, never used as a substitute for this run's result.

Recorded-workflow runtime guards and recipes/runtime.py remain the owners of step matching, claims, dependencies and completion. Mapping preparation returns concrete arguments/private inputs to ordinary admission. The model still chooses calls; permission and execution boundaries are unchanged.

Evidence and troubleshooting boundaries

The mapping integration fixtures cover passive inspection, pause ownership, future-only cases, one-time selection, frozen-input recovery, duplicate-amendment prevention, launch recovery and fresh producer receipts. Task-picker fixtures exercise shared session identity, revision conflicts, delayed pause settlement and completion while choosing a call. RAM authority fixtures exercise correction/recovery without runtime SQLite. The browser fixtures cover per-call entry and task-card selection/recovery on desktop and mobile with isolated responses.

If Apply remains unavailable, inspect readiness before assuming a UI failure: accepted work or an execution lease can still be settling. A stale revision/token requires reopening or previewing again. An applying recovery action reuses saved intent. A suspended mapping requires review. Missing producer evidence blocks the dependent step; the system does not fill the gap from an earlier run or guess a different saved parameter identity.
